Angelic Davis (angelic.davis@enron.com) sent 6 messages to dana.davis@enron.com between 2001-10-01 and 2001-11-01 (end exclusive). Dana Davis is in To or Cc on each of them. I counted each message id once.

ANSWER: 6
SOURCES: Eec51ca95dc10, E78c208665714, Ea4671be47808, Ea9e43a0d11aa, Ef703ce92e611

eSource@ENRON (40enron@enron.com) sent the most messages on 2001-09-05, with 23. It sent 160 messages in September 2001 in total. The next busiest days were 2001-09-28 with 19 and 2001-09-14 with 16.

I only printed one message id, E80e4adf85ec0, which is a September 2001 message from this sender. I didn't check whether it was sent on 2001-09-05.

ANSWER: 2001-09-05
SOURCES: E80e4adf85ec0

In April 2001 (UTC), Vince Kaminski sent the most messages to vkaminski@aol.com. That address was in the To or Cc of 173 of his 458 messages that month. The count is by unique message.

The next most frequent address was his own Enron address, vince.kaminski@enron.com, with 135. Shirley Crenshaw came third with 54.

ANSWER: vkaminski@aol.com
SOURCES: Efdba38023aa8, E6fec8413c70c, E3d11988db63b

Jeff Dasovich sent the most messages to Richard Sanders in that window. I filtered messages sent To or Cc richard.sanders@enron.com from 2001-05-29 up to but not including 2001-06-05. That gave 37 messages, and Dasovich sent 8 of them. Susan Mara was next with 5, then Janette Elbertson with 4.

I didn't check whether any of the 37 were duplicates. The corpus is already deduplicated, so I took each one as a unique message.

ANSWER: jeff.dasovich@enron.com
SOURCES: Ec64a0fe2fe15, Efbeffae21bed, Eb4461cb03bfd, E89c6a95fd0e2, Eaa28b1519008

Vince Kaminski sent the most messages on 2001-04-25, with 47. I counted messages from vince.kaminski@enron.com in April 2001 by UTC date. The next highest days were 2001-04-11 with 37 and 2001-04-27 with 36. I didn't open any individual messages, so I have no message ids to cite.

ANSWER: 2001-04-25
SOURCES:

The message is **Ef817f5aac97c**, "FW: 082501 Enron Confirmation", dated 2001-08-24. Bryant Frihart sent it from bryant.frihart@enron.com. The number appears in the body as "703.227.8777 Phone". A search for the number in other formats found only this one message.

ANSWER: bryant.frihart@enron.com
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c

The only message that mentions ORE-7509 is E2083b9620d07. It was sent on 2002-02-27 by marketing@nymex.com, whose display name is "Exchange Information @ENRON". Its subject is "(CMS-26) NOTICE OF INTENTION TO TRANSFER MEMBERSHIP". The matching line reads "Edward Orenchuk (ORE-7509)". The message sits in the deleted_items folder of custodian shackleton-s.

ANSWER: marketing@nymex.com
SOURCES: E2083b9620d07

Only one has the literal "EB-2934" with a hyphen: the Robin Barbe message.

**Message E2093dccd9417** is the one. Robin Barbe (robin.barbe@enron.com) sent it on 2000-12-05, with the subject "PSEG Meeting". It describes a meeting about 50,000/d at Transco Zone 6, on Tuesday, December 5 at 3:00 p.m., in EB-2934.

My search pattern also matched "EB2934" without the hyphen. Eight other messages mention that room, so the hyphenated form is the only one that fits your reference exactly.

ANSWER: robin.barbe@enron.com
SOURCES: E2093dccd9417

Fourteen distinct sender addresses sent at least one message in November 2001 that contains "Raptor". A case-insensitive grep over the full text of every message, filtered to 2001-11-01 up to 2001-12-01, matched 29 messages. I lowercased the sender addresses and counted the unique ones.

The 14 addresses are:
- surfn.go@americawest.com
- james.derrick@enron.com
- jr..legal@enron.com
- tom.fischbach@enron.com
- christian.yoder@enron.com
- j.kaminski@enron.com
- tim.belden@enron.com
- milagros.velasquez@enron.com
- rick.buy@enron.com
- sean.riordan@enron.com
- vkaminski@aol.com
- no.address@enron.com
- m..schmidt@enron.com
- rakesh.bharati@enron.com

j.kaminski@enron.com and vkaminski@aol.com are counted separately because the question asks for distinct addresses. I didn't check whether they belong to the same person. I also didn't open any messages, so I have no source ids to cite.

ANSWER: 14
SOURCES:

The sender with the most messages containing "Azurix" in that window is enron.announcements@enron.com. I searched all messages from 2000-12-01 up to but not including 2001-01-01 (UTC) for "azurix", case-insensitive, across headers and body. That returned 35 unique messages, and I counted them by sender address.

enron.announcements@enron.com sent 7 of them. The next highest was jeffrey.shankman@enron.com with 5.

I didn't print the IDs of the 7 announcement messages. The only ID I have is E96a5b972d3f6, the first hit in the results, and I didn't check who sent it. It may not support the answer.

ANSWER: enron.announcements@enron.com
SOURCES: E96a5b972d3f6

Of the messages dated 2000-05-01 through 2000-05-31 (UTC), 103 contain "Dynegy" (case-insensitive, headers included). I grepped the full text and counted them by UTC send date. 2000-05-23 had the most, with 14 messages. The next highest were 2000-05-04 and 2000-05-19, with 10 each. The count came from the grep hits themselves, so I didn't open any individual messages. That means I have no message IDs to cite.

ANSWER: 2000-05-23
SOURCES:

The only message that mentions 703-227-8777 is E f817f5aac97c. Its sender is bryant.frihart@enron.com, and it was sent on 2001-08-24. The number appears there as "703.227.8777", with dots instead of hyphens.

A count of messages from that address dated 2001-08-01 up to 2001-09-01 UTC returned 2.

ANSWER: 2
SOURCES: Ef817f5aac97c
